claim: Locize is the official i18next TMS with a runtime backend and native CLI commands; 11 other TMSes integrate but with less depth.
quote: Only Locize has a TMS-side runtime backend (i18next-locize-backend) that fully implements i18next's create() and update() methods.

claim: A June 2026 i18next-cli command chains instrument, extract, Locize setup, and AI auto-translation in one run, replacing export/email/import cycles.
quote: The traditional way: Export -> Email/Upload -> Translate -> Import -> Redeploy. The Locize way: Edit in Locize -> Instantly live in your app.

claim: react-intl's extract-and-compile pipeline is powerful but fiddly; Lingui extract pulls messages into a PO catalog and compile builds an optimized JS module; Tolgee SDK wraps rendered strings for Alt-click in-context editing.
quote: lingui extract scans your code and pulls every message into a catalog, a PO file by default. ... The SDK wraps the strings it renders, so it can map any text on the page back to its translation key.

claim: lingui extract analyzes source code and extracts all messages into per-locale catalogs, merging with existing translations so they survive.
quote: Message extraction is a process of analyzing your code and extracting all messages defined in it, so that your message catalogs are always up-to-date with the source code.

claim: Lingui supports PO (default/recommended), JSON (lingui and minimal styles), and CSV catalog formats; PO supports translator comments, metadata, and contexts.
quote: PO files are translation files used by gettext internationalization system. This is the recommended and the default catalog format in Lingui.

claim: Lingui CLI extracts messages into gettext PO files that are translated via Crowdin and compiled into optimized JSON/JS catalogs, with automated CI/CD sync.
quote: The Lingui CLI extracts messages into Gettext .po files, which are then translated via Crowdin and compiled into optimized JSON/JS catalogs for runtime use.

claim: Crowdin ships a Lingui String Exporter app to handle Lingui PO catalogs on the platform.
quote: Lingui String Exporter - Crowdin Marketplace

claim: inlang ecosystem tools: Paraglide (compiler i18n), inlang CLI (CI/CD automation with machine translation and validation, plugins for JSON/i18next/next-intl), Sherlock VS Code extension, Fink CAT editor, and a macOS i18n editor.
quote: Automate localization tasks in CI/CD pipelines with machine translation, validation, and plugin support for JSON, i18next, next-intl, and more.

claim: Paraglide JS is a compiler-based i18n library emitting tree-shakable translations for up to 70% smaller bundles.
quote: Compiler-based i18n library that emits tree-shakable translations, leading to up to 70% smaller bundle sizes.

claim: Fink lets translators edit messages in a git repo via a web app without cloning the repo or using the git CLI.
quote: Fink makes it easy for translators to work with message files in a git repo, without having to clone the repo or use the git CLI directly.

claim: next-intl uses JSON message files and recommends Crowdin, integrating via Crowdin CLI, GitHub app, webhooks, over-the-air SDK, or manual up/download.
quote: Command-line integration with the Crowdin CLI, Git integration e.g. via the GitHub app, Automatic workflows triggered from webhooks, Over-the-air delivery via the JS SDK, Manual up- and download of messages.

claim: next-intl's experimental useExtracted hook auto-extracts messages from source with no key naming and no CLI, via a Turbopack/Webpack loader during next dev and next build.
quote: Extraction integrates automatically with next dev and next build via a Turbo- or Webpack loader, you don't need to manually trigger it.

claim: useExtracted makes labels eligible for translation with no key naming and no CLI; available experimentally in next-intl@4.5 and needs Next.js 16+.
quote: you can make labels eligible for translation with no naming of keys and no CLI to invoke, just next dev as you're used to.

claim: typesafe-i18n is a fully type-safe zero-dependency i18n library whose generator produces TypeScript definitions in dev mode; it has no built-in TMS.
quote: A fully type-safe and lightweight internationalization library for all your TypeScript and JavaScript projects.

claim: FormatJS CLI extracts message IDs from source into a JSON file to keep messages in sync; a babel plugin/AST transformer auto-inserts IDs since manual IDs are discouraged.
quote: FormatJS provides a CLI to automatically extract message IDs from your source code into a JSON file, ensuring your messages file stays in sync with your components.

claim: @formatjs/cli extracts from defineMessages/FormattedMessage/formatMessage and ships built-in formatters for crowdin, lokalise, smartling, transifex, plus custom formatters.
quote: Built-in formatter names are default, simple, transifex, smartling, lokalise, and crowdin.

claim: Tolgee in-context editing works via Alt+click on any text in the running app, opens a dialog to edit, and functions even in production; one-click screenshot capture adds context.
quote: hold ALT + click on any text element in your running application to instantly open a dialog and modify translations on the fly.

claim: Tolgee integrates DeepL, Google Translate, and AWS Translate out of the box, giving translators instant AI suggestions with app-extracted context.
quote: Tolgee integrates DeepL, Google Translate, and AWS Translate out of the box.

claim: As of mid-2026 official MCP servers ship for Locize, Crowdin, Lokalise, Phrase, POEditor, Tolgee, and SimpleLocalize; BYOK LLM keys supported across most.
quote: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers are now broadly available across i18next-relevant TMSes.

claim: MCP lets AI agents perform localization actions (add keys, create tasks, check progress) in a TMS without API scripts or switching UIs.
quote: MCP (Model Context Protocol) in localization is a standardized way for AI agents to interact with a translation management system.

claim: Ninja i18n is a GitHub lint action that automates i18n linting for pull requests.
quote: Ninja i18n - GitHub Lint Action - Automate your i18n linting for pull requests.

claim: i18n-check validates ICU and i18next translation files, comparing source language to targets to find missing and broken translations in CI.
quote: i18n-check validates your ICU and i18next translation files and checks for missing and broken translations.

claim: A build-time lint step comparing key sets across locale files is the cheap first CI gate, failing on structural parity issues in under a second.
quote: The lint step is the cheap first gate: compare key sets across locale files in CI, fail on structural parity issues. It costs five minutes to configure and runs in under a second.

claim: Teams automate i18n via GitHub Actions using three approaches including missing-translation health checks that fail the build.
quote: How to Automate i18n Translations with GitHub Actions: 3 Approaches.

claim: Weblate is a self-hostable continuous localization platform with tight git integration used by 2500+ libre projects, and supports React Intl JSON among many formats.
quote: Weblate is libre software web-based continuous localization system, used by over 2500 libre projects and companies in more than 165 countries.

claim: Weblate is a web-based localization tool with tight version control integration.
quote: Web based localization tool with tight version control integration.

claim: Tolgee is an open-source, self-hostable Lokalise/Crowdin alternative with native React SDK and in-context editing.
quote: Tolgee vs Crowdin - The Open-Source Lokalise Alternative.

claim: i18next and inlang can interoperate, letting teams keep i18next runtime while using inlang tooling.
quote: You don't have to choose: i18next and inlang, together.

claim: react-intl/FormatJS integrates with TMS platforms like Phrase Strings for the extract-translate-import cycle.
quote: React Localization with react-intl/FormatJS + Phrase Strings.

claim: react-intl formats strings/numbers/dates/plurals using ICU MessageFormat natively.
quote: React-intl uses ICU MessageFormat natively, with plurals, gender-based select, and nested formatting all expressed directly in message strings.
